description: Real-time knowledge tools: weather via Open-Meteo (free, no key) and top news via Google News RSS (free, no auth), wired into the SAME function-calling pipeline as makeCall/openApp so Mayra answers 'aaj weather kaisa hai' and 'aaj ki top news' truthfully instead of hallucinating (user request E). Works when provider=gemini (function-calling is Gemini-only, which is acceptable per the brief). Add the API hosts to the service worker never-cache pass-through. Depends on FEAT-002 (functions.js structure settled) and FEAT-003 (prompt already states she can fetch weather/news and is honest when she can't).
steps: js/functions.js TOOL_DECLARATIONS: add a getWeather tool (name 'getWeather', description in the makeCall style e.g. 'Aaj ka weather / temperature batata hai user ki current location ke hisaab se. Use when user asks aaj weather/mausam kaisa hai, temperature kya hai.', parameters OBJECT with no required properties — location comes from device). Add a getNews tool (name 'getNews', description 'Aaj ki top news headlines laata hai. Use when user asks aaj ki top news, kya ho raha hai India mein, latest khabrein.', parameters OBJECT, optional STRING 'topic' but not required).

js/android-bridge.js: add a getLocation() helper that returns { ok, latitude, longitude } | { ok:false, reason:'denied'|'unavailable' }. Native path: if window.Capacitor.Plugins.Geolocation exists use it; otherwise fall back to navigator.geolocation.getCurrentPosition (wrap in a Promise with a timeout, resolve ok:false on error/denied — never throw). Export getLocation in the public API. NOTE: Capacitor Geolocation plugin may not be installed; if it isn't present, navigator.geolocation inside the WebView still works with the ACCESS_FINE/COARSE_LOCATION manifest perms. Do not add a new npm dependency.

js/functions.js execute(): add `case 'getWeather':` — call AndroidBridge.getLocation(); if not ok/denied, return { ok:false, reason:'location_denied', message:'Weather batane ke liye mujhe location chahiye — Settings mein location allow kar do, phir turant bata dungi ❤️' } (Mayra must NEVER fake weather). If ok, call MayraHTTP.request({ tag:'WEATHER', method:'GET', url: `https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast?latitude=${lat}&longitude=${lon}&current=temperature_2m,weather_code,relative_humidity_2m,wind_speed_10m&timezone=auto` }); parse r.data.current into a compact summary object { ok:true, temperature, humidity, wind, condition } where condition is mapped from weather_code via a small WMO-code->Hinglish/English description map; return it. Guard all parsing so a bad response returns { ok:false, message:'Weather abhi nahi mil paya, thodi der baad try karo.' }.

js/functions.js execute(): add `case 'getNews':` — call MayraHTTP.request({ tag:'NEWS', method:'GET', url:'https://news.google.com/rss?hl=en-IN&gl=IN&ceid=IN:en' }); the response is RSS XML (string). Parse it WITHOUT DOMParser dependency assumptions: prefer DOMParser if available (WebView has it) to read <item><title> nodes; also include a regex fallback that extracts the first ~5 <title> values inside <item> blocks (skipping the channel title). Return { ok:true, headlines:[...up to 5 strings] } or { ok:false, message:'Abhi news nahi laa payi, thodi der baad puchho.' } on any failure. Never fabricate headlines.

js/functions.js buildFollowUpPrompt(): add follow-up handling for getWeather (success -> a short warm line stating temperature + condition, e.g. `Abhi ${result.temperature}°C hai aur ${result.condition} — ${...}`; location_denied -> the warm location-permission line) and getNews (success -> warmly introduce that these are aaj ki top khabrein, the model will summarize from the returned headlines; failure -> warm can't-fetch line). Keep these consistent with existing follow-up style. Since the Gemini follow-up turn re-generates natural text from the function result JSON, the follow-up prompt strings are the fallback used if the follow-up turn fails.

Confirm the chat function-call pipeline (gemini-chat.js _processResponse -> _buildHistoryWithFunctionResults -> follow-up turn) and the voice pipeline (gemini-voice.js msg.toolCall -> execute -> sendFunctionResult) both already dispatch by tool name via MayraFunctions.execute, so getWeather/getNews flow through unchanged. No pipeline edits should be needed beyond adding the cases; verify this by reading both call sites.

sw.js: in the fetch handler's never-cache block, add url.hostname.includes('api.open-meteo.com') and url.hostname.includes('news.google.com') (and any geocoding host if you add one) alongside the existing generativelanguage/groq/openai hosts so these are always fetched live and never cached.

If getWeather/getNews are ever invoked from index.html directly (they are NOT — they run via the model tool pipeline), they'd need App export; they are model-only so no HTML/App export is required. Confirm no HTML wiring is needed.
acceptance_criteria: unset NODE_OPTIONS && node --check passes for js/functions.js, js/android-bridge.js, js/sw.js (sw.js checked too).
functions.js TOOL_DECLARATIONS contains getWeather and getNews; execute() has cases for both; buildFollowUpPrompt handles both.

getWeather returns a location_denied result (never fabricated weather) when location is unavailable, and otherwise calls Open-Meteo via MayraHTTP.request with the exact current= fields and timezone=auto.
getNews fetches Google News RSS via MayraHTTP.request and parses up to 5 <item> titles with a DOMParser-preferred + regex-fallback approach, returning ok:false warmly on failure (never fabricated).
sw.js never-cache pass-through includes api.open-meteo.com and news.google.com.
AndroidBridge.getLocation exists, is exported, uses Capacitor Geolocation if present else navigator.geolocation, and never throws (resolves ok:false on denial/error). No new npm dependency added.
verification: unset NODE_OPTIONS && node --check js/functions.js js/android-bridge.js sw.js (per file).
grep -n 'getWeather\|getNews' js/functions.js and confirm presence in TOOL_DECLARATIONS + execute + buildFollowUpPrompt.
grep -n 'api.open-meteo.com\|news.google.com' sw.js js/functions.js and confirm hosts in the sw.js never-cache block and the correct request URLs in functions.js.
grep -n 'getLocation' js/android-bridge.js js/functions.js and confirm it is defined, exported, and used by getWeather.
Read gemini-chat.js and gemini-voice.js tool-dispatch sites to confirm getWeather/getNews route through MayraFunctions.execute with no pipeline change needed.
findings: Implemented getWeather (Open-Meteo, no key) and getNews (Google News RSS, no auth) as model-only tools in js/functions.js: added both to TOOL_DECLARATIONS (parameters OBJECT, no required; getNews has optional 'topic'), added execute() cases, and buildFollowUpPrompt handling. getWeather calls AndroidBridge.getLocation() first and returns {ok:false, reason:'location_denied', warm Hinglish message} when location is denied/unavailable (never fabricates weather); on success calls MayraHTTP.request with the exact current=temperature_2m,weather_code,relative_humidity_2m,wind_speed_10m&timezone=auto URL and maps weather_code via a WMO_CODES table, guarding all parsing. getNews fetches the RSS string and parses via a DOMParser-preferred + regex-fallback _parseNewsHeadlines() (up to 5 <item> titles, CDATA/entity-decoded, channel title skipped), returning ok:false warmly on any failure. Added getLocation() to js/android-bridge.js (exported): uses window.Capacitor.Plugins.Geolocation if present else navigator.geolocation wrapped in a Promise with a 12s safety timeout; never throws (resolves {ok:false, reason:'denied'|'unavailable'}). No npm dependency added. sw.js never-cache pass-through now includes api.open-meteo.com and news.google.com alongside the LLM hosts. Confirmed chat pipeline (gemini-chat.js line 198 MayraFunctions.execute + line 204 buildFollowUpPrompt) and voice pipeline (app.js lines 524-526 via GeminiVoice.onFunctionCall -> MayraFunctions.execute -> sendFunctionResult + buildFollowUpPrompt) dispatch by tool name, so no pipeline edits needed. Static verification only (INTEGRATIONS_ONLY, no network/device): node --check passed for functions.js, android-bridge.js, sw.js; greps confirm all wiring. WEATHER/NEWS tags flow through MayraHTTP._debugLog for on-device confirmation.
